mainEntity.name: How do demountable glass office fronts compare to permanent drywall partitions for sound privacy?

acceptedAnswer.text: Solid construction offers superior sound isolation, whereas demountable glass systems offer light transfer and future layout flexibility. Traditional stud-and-drywall partitions packed with mineral wool achieve high Sound Transmission Class (STC) ratings at a predictable cost, but they are permanent. Modular double-glazed partition systems can match moderate sound ratings and preserve visual openness, yet they require specialized seals and carry a higher material investment. If absolute confidential privacy is your priority, insulated double-stud or multi-layer drywall remains the industry standard.
